chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Any man who has illicit intercourse with a woman, then decides to marry her lawfully, the first part is fornication and the last part is marriage. His example is like that of a palm tree: a man takes its fruit illicitly, then buys it later, and it becomes lawful for him.'
And it is not appropriate for him to marry her after the illicit intercourse unless he waits for her to purify her womb (complete the 'Iddah').

key_terms.اسْتِبْرَاء: Purification (waiting period to ensure no pregnancy)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man marrying a woman he previously had illicit relations with?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that illicit fornication (Zina) does not inherently prohibit subsequent marriage, using the analogy of illicitly taking fruit and then purchasing it to illustrate the transition from sin to lawful union. However, he stipulates that the man must wait for the woman to complete her Istibra (period of waiting to ensure she is not pregnant) before finalizing the marriage, ensuring the removal of any lingering legal or biological impediments. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the act of Zina and the contractual validity of Nikah, emphasizing purification of lineage over permanent prohibition.
